profiles.title: Codex / OpenAI tool-calling
profiles.summary: Bootstrap pack for OpenAI-compatible tool calling, including Codex-style agent loops.
instructions: Use descriptor.tools as the callable contract and do not invent tools outside the NextStat descriptor.
Keep deterministic execution on by default for reproducible scientific workflows unless the user explicitly asks for stochastic runs.

runnable_example.local_purpose: Runnable Codex/OpenAI local bootstrap that prints an OpenAI-compatible tool-calling request payload from the canonical local descriptor.
runnable_example.server_purpose: Runnable Codex/OpenAI server bootstrap that prints an OpenAI-compatible tool-calling request payload from the authenticated server descriptor.

instructions: Prefer local transport when the analysis needs the full Python registry, including ROOT ingest and non-HEP verticals.

snippets.bootstrap:
from nextstat.tools import get_toolkit_descriptor
descriptor = get_toolkit_descriptor(transport="local")
tools = descriptor["tools"]
guidance = descriptor["guidance"]
snippets.execution_loop: Use the OpenAI-compatible descriptor.tools list directly. When the model emits a tool call, validate the arguments against the chosen function schema and execute with nextstat.tools.execute_tool(..., transport="local").

instructions: Prefer server transport when the workflow should stay auth-enabled and remote through nextstat-server.

snippets.bootstrap:
from nextstat.tools import get_toolkit_descriptor
descriptor = get_toolkit_descriptor(transport="server", server_url=server_url, api_key=api_key)
tools = descriptor["tools"]
guidance = descriptor["guidance"]
snippets.execution_loop: Use descriptor.tools as the only callable server-safe subset. Execute tool calls with nextstat.tools.execute_tool(..., transport="server", server_url=..., api_key=..., fallback_to_local=False) when you need strict remote behavior.

profiles.title: Gemini function-calling
profiles.summary: Bootstrap pack for Gemini-style function calling using the same canonical NextStat descriptor.
instructions: Map descriptor.tools into Gemini function declarations without changing tool names or argument schemas.
Use descriptor.guidance.recipes as prompt seeds so the model stays aligned with the intended transport surface.

runnable_example.local_purpose: Runnable Gemini local bootstrap that prints a function-calling request payload from the canonical local descriptor.
runnable_example.server_purpose: Runnable Gemini server bootstrap that prints a function-calling request payload from the authenticated server descriptor.

instructions: Local transport is the broadest surface and should be the default when the Gemini workflow runs inside a trusted Python environment.

snippets.execution_loop: Present function_declarations to Gemini, then execute approved calls with nextstat.tools.execute_tool(..., transport="local"). Use descriptor.guidance.hints to explain local-only capabilities when the workflow needs broader coverage.

instructions: Server transport keeps Gemini on the server-safe subset and is the right default for remote/shared deployments.

snippets.execution_loop: Only expose descriptor.tools to Gemini. When a call is selected, execute it remotely with nextstat.tools.execute_tool(..., transport="server", server_url=..., api_key=..., fallback_to_local=False).

profiles.title: Anthropic / Claude tool use
profiles.summary: Bootstrap pack for Anthropic Claude tool use using a provider-native messages plus tools request shape.
instructions: Map descriptor.tools into Anthropic tool definitions without renaming tools or mutating argument schemas.
Keep the system prompt concise and use descriptor.guidance.recipes as the workflow layer instead of embedding long procedural prompts.

runnable_example.local_purpose: Runnable Claude local bootstrap that prints an Anthropic-native messages plus tools request payload from the canonical local descriptor.
runnable_example.server_purpose: Runnable Claude server bootstrap that prints an Anthropic-native messages plus tools request payload from the authenticated server descriptor.

instructions: Use local transport when the Claude workflow runs inside a trusted Python environment and needs the full local NextStat descriptor.

snippets.execution_loop: Expose descriptor.tools as Anthropic tool definitions, keep descriptor.guidance.recipes as the workflow layer, and execute approved calls with nextstat.tools.execute_tool(..., transport="local").

instructions: Use server transport for remote or shared Claude workflows so the callable surface stays aligned with the authenticated server-safe subset.

snippets.execution_loop: Only expose descriptor.tools to Claude, then execute approved calls with nextstat.tools.execute_tool(..., transport="server", server_url=..., api_key=..., fallback_to_local=False).

profiles.title: Ollama / local open-weight models
profiles.summary: Bootstrap pack for local models that may use MCP or a manual validated tool loop instead of first-class function calling.
instructions: Do not assume the model can emit perfect function calls; keep a validated manual loop available.
Use descriptor.capabilities to explain unavailable tools instead of silently substituting local-only functionality.

runnable_example.local_purpose: Runnable Ollama local bootstrap that prints a manual-tool-loop request payload from the canonical local descriptor.
runnable_example.server_purpose: Runnable Ollama server bootstrap that prints a manual-tool-loop request payload from the authenticated server descriptor.

instructions: For trusted local automation, use the full local descriptor and, if needed, get_mcp_tools() as the MCP-facing mirror.

snippets.execution_loop: If the local model lacks reliable function calling, ask it to choose a tool name plus JSON arguments, validate that pair against descriptor.tools, then execute with nextstat.tools.execute_tool(..., transport="local").

instructions: For remote/shared use, keep Ollama on the server-safe subset and disable local fallback when strict server execution matters.

snippets.execution_loop: Run a validated manual tool loop over descriptor.tools and execute with nextstat.tools.execute_tool(..., transport="server", server_url=..., api_key=..., fallback_to_local=False). Treat descriptor.guidance.recipes as the workflow prompt layer.

profiles.title: MCP tool server
profiles.summary: Bootstrap pack for Model Context Protocol tool servers using the canonical NextStat tool and guidance surfaces.
instructions: Use MCP tool definitions as the protocol surface, but keep descriptor.guidance.recipes as workflow and prompt seeds.
Keep MCP tool names and input schemas aligned with the canonical NextStat tool manifest; do not invent aliases.

runnable_example.local_purpose: Runnable MCP local bootstrap that prints an MCP tool-server config from the canonical local MCP mirror plus descriptor guidance.
runnable_example.server_purpose: Runnable MCP server bootstrap that prints an MCP tool-server config derived from the authenticated server descriptor.

instructions: For trusted local automation, build the MCP tool list from nextstat.tools.get_mcp_tools() and dispatch through nextstat.tools.handle_mcp_call().

snippets.bootstrap: from nextstat.tools import get_mcp_tools, get_toolkit_descriptor\nmcp_tools = get_mcp_tools()\ndescriptor = get_toolkit_descriptor(transport="local")
snippets.execution_loop: Expose mcp_tools through your MCP server or bridge, then dispatch validated calls with nextstat.tools.handle_mcp_call(name, arguments). Use descriptor.guidance.recipes as the workflow layer.

instructions: For remote/shared use, derive MCP tool definitions from get_toolkit_descriptor(transport="server", ...) so the protocol surface stays restricted to the authenticated server-safe subset.

snippets.bootstrap: descriptor = get_toolkit_descriptor(transport="server", server_url=server_url, api_key=api_key)\nmcp_tools = [{"name": tool["function"]["name"], "description": tool["function"]["description"], "inputSchema": tool["function"]["parameters"]} for tool in descriptor["tools"]]
snippets.execution_loop: Expose the derived mcp_tools through your MCP bridge, then dispatch approved calls with nextstat.tools.execute_tool(..., transport="server", server_url=..., api_key=..., fallback_to_local=False).

profiles.title: IDE assistant / copilot rules
profiles.summary: Bootstrap pack for editor-integrated assistants that need short workspace-safe rules and transport-aware recipes.
instructions: Treat the descriptor as the canonical source when authoring IDE rules, snippets, or assistant instructions.
Prefer short, transport-aware workspace rules instead of long narrative prompts.

workspace_outputs.purpose: Repo-native Copilot instructions generated from the canonical workspace-output bootstrap profile.
Cursor rule file generated from the same workspace-output bootstrap profile and transport-aware guidance.

instructions: Local IDE rules may mention the full Python registry, including ROOT ingest and non-HEP verticals.

snippets.bootstrap: Workspace rule seed: 'Load the local NextStat descriptor first, use descriptor.tools as the callable surface, and use descriptor.guidance.recipes as task templates.'
snippets.execution_loop: If the IDE assistant proposes a tool call, validate it against descriptor.tools and prefer deterministic execution for code review, notebooks, and reproducible analyses.

instructions: Server IDE rules must describe the restricted subset explicitly so the assistant does not hallucinate local-only tools.

snippets.bootstrap: Workspace rule seed: 'For remote NextStat usage, only use descriptor.tools from get_toolkit_descriptor(transport="server", ...); use descriptor.capabilities to explain why local-only tools are unavailable.'
snippets.execution_loop: Keep IDE instructions short: audit with descriptor.guidance.recipes, execute through nextstat.tools.execute_tool(..., transport="server", server_url=..., api_key=..., fallback_to_local=False), and avoid local fallback when strict remote behavior is required.
